title: File VEC-ROOT-001: the eligibility block defines 'body' in photograph terms
intent: File the primary finding from the 2026-09-19 vectorizer investigation into the repository, where it is currently untracked. It records that the eligibility block at services/photo-vectorizer/edge_to_dxf.py:941-950 encodes three assumptions true of a photographed subject and false of a drawn one, and discards the body on both plans measured, by two different branches. Includes a positive control on the input class the tool was built for, and a corpus census taken before any fix is scoped. Documentation only: one new Markdown file, no code.
behavior_change: None. One new Markdown file under docs/audit/ plus this manifest. No code, configuration, workflow or test is touched. The document proposes NO fix -- sections 5 and 7 state this explicitly -- and authorizes no implementation.

diff_articulation.what_changed: Adds docs/audit/VEC-ROOT-001_eligibility_body_definition.md. Section 0 states the lineage boundary: everything concerns edge_to_dxf.py only, and D-13 is a vectorizer_phase3.py artifact that this document does NOT explain. Section 1 sets out the three premises the eligibility block encodes. Section 2 carries two instrumented censuses -- the cuatro dies at too_small (943), L-00 at child_contour (947). Section 3 records that rejecting a contour does not unparent what sits inside it. Section 11 is the positive control: the archtop, an AI-generated image, passes eligibility at 0.8464 on the background-removed input, confirming the premises by positive evidence rather than failure analysis alone. Section 11a records that passing is not constructibility -- the eligible contour weaves between neck edge and inlay blocks, which explains the April decision to stop. Section 13 is a corpus census run before scoping any fix.
diff_articulation.why_not_redundant: The finding exists only as an untracked file in the owner's Downloads directory. The forensic audit merged in PR #385 records D-13's measurement and withdraws its attribution, but carries none of the eligibility-block analysis, neither census, the archtop control, nor the corpus census. Nothing in the repository currently records why the body is discarded.

commands_run: Instrumented extract_blueprint_to_dxf(isolate_body=True) on the cuatro and on Gibson-L0-IN.png, 2026-09-19, by wrapping _build_hierarchy_nodes and _score_contour_group at runtime. No repo file was edited by any run.
Cuatro per stage: 7,368 findContours -> 7,368 after border removal -> 7,332 nodes -> 3 eligible. Refusals 7,328 too_small, 1 child_contour. Lower bout: 1,437 contours, 0 eligible.

L-00: 3,053 contours, 0 eligible, run returns 'No valid contours found in edge image'. Largest contour 1815x1365 px encloses 0.276 of the raster -- 55x the 0.005 floor -- and is refused as child_contour.

Archtop control through the same path: 488 contours, 1 eligible at area_ratio 0.0145 with parent None, winner score 0.8464 on the background-removed input and 0.9894 on the original. Rendered and confirmed to be the guitar.
Every claim tagged [RENDER] rests on drawing the result onto the source image and looking, per the standing rule written after the soundhole retraction (30b8a5db).
Corpus census: 314 distinct PDFs opened read-only with PyMuPDF; 215 VECTOR, 5 MIXED, 41 RASTER, 50 EMPTY, 3 ERROR. The cuatro and L-00 are both RASTER; Carlos Jumbo 3-3 is VECTOR with 76,063 paths.

files.intent: Record why the body is discarded, with the lineage boundary stated first so the finding is not carried into vectorizer_phase3.py, and with the dead ends recorded so they are not retried: convex hull re-introduces an area assumption, and arc length ranks a ruled fret table fifth.
files.behavior_change: None - audit record. The document proposes no replacement primitive and no fix, and states so in sections 5 and 7. Section 8 gives outcome criteria any future fix must satisfy; it does not authorize one.
